newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent slips as U.S.-bound cargo play ends.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent slips as U.S.-bound cargo play ends.

text.p: North Sea cash crude markets drifted lower as Brent physical trade ran out of steam after a big buyer filled his U.S. Gulf-bound ULCC, traders said.
Short-term swaps for next week (July 14-18) began the day offered at 12 cents under September but were several cents lower by midday. Weeks further out also slipped lower.
Physical business was thinly discussed, with players trying to work out the participants in a number of private deals concluded on Wednesday, as outright prices drifted lower on technical factors.
At 1230 GMT IPE Brent contracts for August were 15 cents lower at $18.07 a barrel.

A Brent loading July 23-25 moved from a trader to either a Norwegian or a French buyer at August Brent "plus a lot," dealers said. The previous Brent deal, also on Wednesday, was done at August +10 cents a barrel.

The Norwegian buyer was now believed to have filled the ULCC he fixed for July 21, with purchasers for the contents already lined up. Brent prices may now slip but a tight physical market should provide a floor, dealers added.
One cargo, loading July 25-27, is due to turn wet from the paper chains on Thursday.
Late July Oseberg and Gullfaks A cargoes were also believed traded on Wednesday but prices were being kept from the market.
A smattering of July cargoes was all that was left from the month, with traders beginning to think of next month loading programmes, and some strength in the northern sour market.

"So far people are just watching and waiting today, though things seem slightly weaker," said one broker. A trader was heard to have bought Baltic sour barrels loading July 23-25 at 20 cents below Dated Brent, basis Rotterdam.
